report:
## Conclusion

The scientific evidence does **not** support the claim that hydroxychloroquine reduces the risk of dying from COVID-19. In fact, the best available data suggest it provides no mortality benefit and may even be associated with slightly worse outcomes.

**What the evidence shows:**

- **RECOVERY trial** (UK, >11,000 hospitalized patients, one of the largest randomized controlled trials): found "no significant difference" in 28-day mortality between hydroxychloroquine and standard care, prompting investigators to halt that arm and declare "it doesn't work" (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2022926).

- **WHO Solidarity Trial** (multi-country RCT, thousands of hospitalized patients): concluded hydroxychloroquine "appeared to have little or no effect" on 28-day in-hospital mortality, ventilation initiation, or hospital stay duration (https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019/global-research-on-novel-coronavirus-2019-ncov/solidarity-clinical-trial-for-covid-19-treatments/interim-results).

- **PRINCIPLE trial** (UK community-based platform RCT in older patients) similarly evaluated hydroxychloroquine's effectiveness and found no benefit for the outcomes studied (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-09275-6).

- A large international **collaborative meta-analysis of randomized trials** published in Nature Communications went further, finding that hydroxychloroquine treatment was actually **associated with increased mortality** in COVID-19 patients, with no benefit and some signal of harm (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-22446-z).

**Bottom line:** Multiple large, well-conducted randomized controlled trials (RECOVERY, Solidarity, PRINCIPLE) and pooled meta-analyses consistently show hydroxychloroquine does not reduce COVID-19 mortality — and some analyses suggest possible increased risk. This is why the WHO and other health authorities discontinued its use for COVID-19 treatment. Earlier hopeful data typically came from smaller, non-randomized, or flawed observational studies, which don't hold up against rigorous trial evidence. Your sister's belief isn't supported by current high-quality evidence.
